comparator.name: Dutch Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product accounts for 180 EC: a 60-EC first-year core, 30 EC of second-year compulsory work, 50 EC of internal specialisation study spanning years two and three, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC open elective space. The Dutch Linguistics specialisation group is instantiated because it most directly preserves the programme’s broad Dutch-language identity; its two 10-EC compulsory courses and the first three eligible 10-EC listed choices make the required 50 EC. This choice is made independently of UCR fit. The 0-EC mentoring and thesis-seminar modules are omitted. The 2026–27 programme-specific OER states that formal graduation directions are not applicable, so routeSelection is null even though the study product organises the 50-EC bound-choice space into internal specialisation groups.

exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent the defining Dutch-specific language, linguistics, literature, media and historical-text curriculum of Leiden’s Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. UCR offers one introductory Dutch language course but no Dutch-language progression, Dutch linguistics sequence, Dutch literature sequence or sustained study of Dutch cultural texts. A schedule filled with general rhetoric, literature, media and history would change the target into general communication and cultural studies and falsely imply Dutch disciplinary preparation.
exception.curriculumContext: The complete 180-EC comparator contains 60 EC of foundational Dutch language, literature, rhetoric and media study; 30 EC of compulsory second-year disciplinary work; a 50-EC Dutch Linguistics specialisation choice; a 10-EC Dutch-linguistics thesis; and 30 EC open electives. The internal linguistics choice remains embedded in a programme whose common core covers older and modern Dutch literature, the history and social use of Dutch, Dutch media and historical Dutch texts. The OER does not recognize formal graduation directions, hence routeSelection is null.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is a single introductory language course focused on uncomplicated everyday communication; it is not an academic Dutch sequence. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics examines general language processing and cognition, while MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication, MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning, MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication and MCCCOMM213 Rhetoric in Action provide general rhetoric and communication methods. MCCLITR111/112/311/312 offer broad literary analysis, and MCCMEDI111/112/211/311 offer general media study. None provides sustained Dutch linguistics, historical Dutch, Dutch literary history or Dutch-language primary-source work. These courses can support adjacent questions but cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Dutch Language and Culture rationale or reproduce the comparator’s disciplinary progression.
